span_decisions.rationale: Real readonly descriptor preserves the same public FILE/closer/default stream while causing repeated buffered flush failure. C captured native counterpart executes first write/flush/second write/flush/close and ownership checks.

Darwin native fclose retries pending buffered bytes and returns error while closing FILE. Replacement requires nil/message/positive errno and closed userdata identity, preserving physical cleanup rather than falsely requiring success.

Same real descriptor supplies unbuffered zero-byte refusal; original following POSIX T.nonblock pipe/receiver path stays untouched. Counterpart checks zero transferred bytes, successful unbuffered close and closed identity.

Actual C diagnostic reports directHUP=nil,signal,1 and directKILL=nil,signal,9 for both APIs; original nestedHUP returns signal1, whereas explicit outer-shell wait returns exit129. Trailing status/exit keeps outer shell alive, preserving intended nested-child-exit distinction. Three counterpart checks enforce exact triples; no dynamic expected value or broad skip.

Observed Darwin max-tm_year seconds60/61 discard day carry and normalize to December31 midnight/00:00:01 instead of rejecting. Counterpart checks exact relative timestamps (-86399/-86398), all normalized/reverse calendar fields, reverse os.time identity, direct next-year exact field rejection and ordinary conversion recovery. This is an explicit native divergence, never an unchanged upstream error-test pass.
